hook: Twenty small purchases quietly became five hundred dollars, and none of them felt like a decision.

sections.voiceover: Twenty small purchases quietly became five hundred dollars by the end of the month. Each one felt too small to matter at the time.
Left on a credit card, that balance grew from five hundred dollars to eight hundred and forty dollars, because interest compounds every single month.
Paying the minimum costs three hundred and forty dollars in interest, but clearing it in full costs nothing at all.
The purchases were never the problem. The balance you carry between months is what actually costs you.
